formats.key: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
effects: Sets the Safe's owners to `_owners` and the confirmation threshold to `_threshold` (once only).
Sets `fallbackHandler` as the fallback handler when it is not zero.
Always delegatecalls `to` with `data` in the Safe's context. This code can enable modules, change owners or move funds.
When `payment` > 0, sends `payment` of `paymentToken` (ETH when zero) from the Safe to `paymentReceiver`, or to tx.origin when that is zero.
formats.shown: "Setup Safe" with the signers, the raw threshold, the fallback handler, the payment amount in its token, the payment receiver, and `data` decoded as a call to `to` under the label "Module".

findings.title: setup decodes the `data` field as a normal call to `to`, but the code always delegatecalls it.
findings.evidence: ModuleManager.setupModules: `if (!execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, type(uint256).max))`. Descriptor setup field `data`: {"label":"Module","format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to"}}. Nothing on screen says it is a delegate call.
findings.fix: Label the field "Delegate call (runs in the Safe)". Add a visible `to` field labelled "Setup delegate call target". Change the intent to say that setup code runs in the Safe.

findings.title: setup labels arbitrary delegatecall setup data as "Module", but it does not just enable a module.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "label": "Module" on path `data`. Safe.setup calls setupModules(to, data), which runs any delegatecall payload.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Setup call" or "Delegate call".

findings.title: setup shows a zero payment receiver literally, but the code then pays tx.origin.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. Descriptor field `paymentReceiver` is a plain addressName.
findings.fix: Add `senderAddress` set to the zero address on `paymentReceiver`, or label it "Payment receiver (zero = transaction sender)".

findings.title: setup intent "Setup Safe" does not mention the payment or the delegatecall.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Setup Safe". Safe.setup also calls handlePayment(payment, ...) and setupModules(to, data).
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Set up Safe with {_threshold} threshold, pay {payment}".

formats.key: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
effects: Sends msg.value of native currency from the signer (executor) to the Safe; the function is payable.
The Safe calls `to` with `value` of native currency and `data`, or delegatecalls `to` when `operation` is 1. The delegatecall runs `to`'s code with the Safe's balances and storage.
Increments the Safe nonce and uses the Safe transaction hash that the owners signed.

When gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice in `gasToken` (ETH when zero, price capped at tx.gasprice) to `refundReceiver`, or to tx.origin when that is zero. gasUsed is bounded by `safeTxGas`.
Calls the Safe's transaction guard before and after execution, when a guard is set.
formats.shown: "sign multisig operation" with the operation type, the Safe, the executor, the nested call decoded for `to` (the inner value is passed only to the nested descriptor), raw base gas, gas price in gasToken and the gas receiver. safeTxGas, signatures and msg.value are not shown.

findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction is `external payable`. The descriptor execTransaction fields have no `@.value` path, and nothing in the code forces msg.value to zero.

findings.title: execTransaction never shows the inner `to` and `value` as fields, so a plain ETH send shows nothing.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction: `execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)` → Executor `call(txGas, to, value, ...)`. In the descriptor, `to` and `value` appear only as calleePath/amountPath of the `data` calldata field. When `data` is empty, nothing shows the ETH that leaves the Safe or who receives it.
findings.fix: Add {"path":"to","label":"To","format":"addressName","visible":"always"} and {"path":"value","label":"Value","format":"amount","visible":"always"}. Mention both in an interpolatedIntent.

findings.title: execTransaction decodes nested calldata as a call to `to`, even when the operation is a delegate call.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, ...) }`. The descriptor `data` field uses {"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"} for both operations. The enum shows "Delegate Call", but the nested screen describes an outcome for `to` that does not happen.
findings.fix: Make the nested decode depend on operation == 0. For operation 1, show a warning label such as "Delegate call: code runs in your Safe" with `to` visible. Or restrict delegate calls to known targets such as MultiSend.

findings.title: execTransaction intent says "sign multisig operation", but the call executes the Safe transaction.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "sign multisig operation". Safe.execTransaction checks signatures and then runs `execute(...)` and handlePayment.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Execute Safe transaction" and add an interpolatedIntent naming `to` and `value`.

findings.title: execTransaction hides safeTxGas, which bounds the gas refund the Safe pays.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction: `execute(..., gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas)` and `payment = handlePayment(gasUsed, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver)`. Descriptor: {"path":"safeTxGas","visible":"never"}.
findings.fix: Show safeTxGas as "Safe tx gas limit" when gasPrice > 0. Or show a computed maximum refund label.

findings.title: execTransaction labels baseGas "Gas amount" and gasPrice as a token amount, so neither reads as the total refund.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: baseGas label "Gas amount" (raw), gasPrice label "Gas price" (tokenAmount with gasToken). Safe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)`.
findings.fix: Rename baseGas to "Base gas (refunded)" and gasPrice to "Refund price per gas".

findings.title: execTransaction shows a zero refundReceiver literally, but the refund then goes to tx.origin.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver`. Descriptor field `refundReceiver` is a plain addressName.
findings.fix: Add `senderAddress` set to the zero address, or a label that explains that zero means the executor.

effects: Adds `owner` as a new Safe owner (callable only by the Safe itself).
Sets the threshold to `_threshold` when it differs from the current one.
formats.shown: "Add signer" with the new signer and the new threshold.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold limits the owner address type to eoa, but the code accepts contract owners.
findings.evidence: Descriptor owner params {"types":["eoa"]}. OwnerManager.addOwnerWithThreshold rejects only zero, the sentinel and the Safe itself.

findings.title: addOwnerWithThreshold intent "Add signer" leaves out the threshold change.

effects: Removes `owner` from the Safe owners (callable only by the Safe itself).
Sets the threshold to `_threshold` when it differs from the current one.
formats.shown: "Remove signer" with the signer removed and the new threshold. prevOwner, a linked-list pointer, is hidden.

findings.title: removeOwner intent "Remove signer" leaves out the threshold change.

formats.key: swapOwner(address prevOwner, address oldOwner, address newOwner)
effects: Replaces Safe owner `oldOwner` with `newOwner` (callable only by the Safe itself). The threshold does not change.
formats.shown: "Swap signer" with the old signer and the new signer.

findings.title: swapOwner limits the new owner address type to eoa, but the code accepts contract owners.
findings.evidence: Descriptor newOwner params {"types":["eoa"]}. OwnerManager.swapOwner rejects only zero, the sentinel and the Safe itself.

effects: Sets the Safe's confirmation threshold to `_threshold` (callable only by the Safe itself).
formats.shown: "Modify threshold" with the new threshold as a raw number.

findings.title: changeThreshold cannot show the owner count, so the threshold has no "of N" context.
findings.evidence: OwnerManager.changeThreshold reads `ownerCount` from storage. The descriptor shows only `_threshold` raw.

effects: Permanently marks `hashToApprove` as approved by the signer (an owner). This counts as the signer's signature on that Safe transaction or message, and it cannot be revoked.
formats.shown: "Approve Safe hash" with the hash shown raw.

findings.title: approveHash shows a raw hash that stands for a whole Safe transaction the signer cannot see.
findings.evidence: Safe.approveHash: `approvedHashes[msg.sender][hashToApprove] = 1;`. checkNSignatures accepts it as the owner's signature (v == 1). Descriptor field `hashToApprove` is raw.

findings.title: approveHash intent does not say the approval counts as a signature and is permanent.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Approve Safe hash". devdoc: "The approved hash stays approved forever. There's no revocation mechanism".
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Sign Safe tx by hash (permanent)".

findings.format: setup(address[] _owners, uint256 _threshold, address to, bytes data, address fallbackHandler, address paymentToken, uint256 payment, address paymentReceiver)
findings.title: setup decodes the `data` field as a normal call to `to`, but the code always delegatecalls it.
findings.reason: Whenever `to` is non-zero, setup always delegatecalls `to`, so `to`'s code runs in the Safe's own context. The descriptor decodes `data` as a plain call to `to`. The only label is "Module", and no field or intent says the call is a delegate call. The guide's examples list exactly this case as critical: nested calldata decoded as a call when it actually runs as a delegate call.
findings.quote: ModuleManager.setupModules (called from Safe.setup): `if (!execute(to, 0, data, Enum.Operation.DelegateCall, type(uint256).max)) revertWithError("GS000");`. Descriptor, setup format: {"path":"data","label":"Module","format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to"}}

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction is payable, but no field shows the native value the signer sends.
findings.reason: execTransaction is payable and no require forces msg.value to zero. Any ETH the signer sends goes into the Safe, and the same call can pass it on through `execute(to, value, ...)`. No field shows @.value, so this matches the guide's payable-function critical.
findings.quote: Safe.execTransaction: `) external payable override returns (bool success) {`, and nothing in the body checks msg.value. Later `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)` spends from the Safe's balance. Descriptor execTransaction fields: operation, @.to, @.from, data, baseGas, gasPrice, refundReceiver, safeTxGas (never), signatures (never). There is no @.value field.

findings.format: execTransaction(address to, uint256 value, bytes data, uint8 operation, uint256 safeTxGas, uint256 baseGas, uint256 gasPrice, address gasToken, address refundReceiver, bytes signatures)
findings.title: execTransaction never shows the inner `to` and `value` as fields, so a plain ETH send shows nothing.
findings.reason: The inner `value` only reaches the screen if a nested descriptor chooses to show it. When `data` is empty there is no selector and no nested descriptor, so nothing shows the ETH that leaves the Safe. No outer field shows `value` either, and at best the spec's MAY fallback shows the callee. Not-critical case 2 needs a separate value field and case 5 needs the amount shown elsewhere; neither is present here.
findings.quote: Safe.execTransaction: `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)`. Descriptor field data: {"format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"}}. Spec erc-7730.md: amountPath 'If provided, the ERC-7730 descriptor for this embedded calldata MAY reference this value using the `@.value` container path'.
